title: Unsynchronized Flag Read in Signal Handler
pattern: Reading or writing plain shared variables from within an asynchronous signal handler concurrently with the main thread.
why_bad: Signals interrupt execution arbitrarily. Writing to a non-`sig_atomic_t` variable inside a signal handler is not guaranteed to be atomic or visible to the main thread, leading to torn reads, missing state changes, or compiler-reordering optimization bugs.
detection: A signal handler writing to a non-`volatile sig_atomic_t` or non-atomic variable that is accessed by the main thread.
fix:
Use `volatile sig_atomic_t` or platform atomic flags.
```c
volatile sig_atomic_t stop_flag = 0;
```
source: Steve McConnell Ch 13, Secure Systems Ch 13
